# encrypted_spp_over_spw: build brief

Encrypted packets over SpaceWire: the OpenCrypto framer cuts every input packet (for example a compressed image) into chunks, the AES-GCM core encrypts every chunk with a generated IV and a 4-byte position in the AAD, and OpenSPP sends every encrypted chunk as one Space Packet through an N-Char adapter and an OpenWire port.

This brief was generated by the Open Space Composer from the system file `encrypted_spp_over_spw.composer.json` (catalog `653fe9bd682c`).
The file holds the system as edited (`instances`, `connections`, `externals`), in `resolved` the netlist it resolves to and in `catalogSubset` the catalog entries of its blocks (interfaces, fields, clocks, generics).
Build a VHDL-2008 top level `encrypted_spp_over_spw` from `resolved` as described below; everything needed is in the file and in the listed repositories.
The button Export HDL of the Composer, and `tools/composer_hdl.mjs` of the repository of the website, write this top level, its compile order and its constraints from the same netlist (`encrypted_spp_over_spw.vhd`, `encrypted_spp_over_spw_compile_order.txt`, `encrypted_spp_over_spw.xdc`, `encrypted_spp_over_spw_top.xdc`); use them, or build the top level by hand as described here.

External interfaces:

- `frm0.S_In` (Byte stream, clock domain `sys`): Byte stream with keep and last and no side band: byte 0 of a beat in data bits 7:0, keep contiguous from byte 0 and partial only on the last beat of a packet.
- `ocr0.S_AxiLite` (AXI4-Lite register bus, clock domain `sys`): AXI4-Lite register access (32 bit data), for example the register file of a core.
- `spp0.M_Rx[0]` (Space Packet receive port, clock domain `sys`): Receive port of OpenSPP: one SDU or Space Packet per stream packet, with APID, flags, loss indicator and the user application value in user.
  - `rx0_M_Rx_User_0`: 10:0 APID; 11 Secondary Header Indicator (Octet String Service); 12 Packet Loss or Data Loss Indicator; 13 Double bit error in the receive buffer during this SDU, valid with last; 21:14 User Application value of the CPTP packet (0 without the CPTP layer).
- `spp0.S_AxiLite` (AXI4-Lite register bus, clock domain `sys`): AXI4-Lite register access (32 bit data), for example the register file of a core.
- `spw0.S_AxiLite` (AXI4-Lite register bus, clock domain `sys`): AXI4-Lite register access (32 bit data), for example the register file of a core.
- `spw0.Spw` (SpaceWire line, clock domain `link`): Data-strobe line drivers and receivers of a SpaceWire link (LVDS buffers outside the core).

## 3. Architecture

1. Context clause (`resolved.context`): `library ieee;` `use ieee.std_logic_1164.all;` `library olo;` `library openwire;` `library openspp;` `library opencrypto;`
2. Declare every signal of `resolved.signals` (one per port of an instance, named `<instance>_<port>_s`, with the type of the port).
3. Instantiate every entry of `resolved.instances` as `i_<id> : entity <library>.<entity>`: a generic map with every generic (the value is the VHDL literal in `vhdl`, package constants fully qualified; write the defaults too, where `default` is true, so that a new default of a core cannot change the system unnoticed), and a port map with the `actual` of every port. Leave out the ports with `useDefault` (they keep their VHDL `default`). Clocks and resets are port actuals on purpose: never assign a clock to another signal.
4. Write every entry of `resolved.nets` as a concurrent assignment `<to> <= <from>;`. They connect the interfaces signal by signal (a packed data word bit by bit), set the side band constants and tie-offs, and connect the top-level ports.

| Instance | Entity | Library | Origin | Clock domain | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frm0` | `ocr_framer` | `opencrypto` | placed | sys |  |
| `ocr0` | `ocr_core` | `opencrypto` | placed | sys |  |
| `spp0` | `spp_core` | `openspp` | placed | sys |  |
| `nchar0` | `spp_nchar` | `openspp` | placed | sys |  |
| `spw0` | `owr_core` | `openwire` | placed | sys |  |
| `auto_rst_sys` | `olo_base_reset_gen` | `olo` | inserted: reset | sys | Synchronous reset of System clock. |

Generics that differ from the VHDL default:

- `frm0`: none
- `ocr0`: `ReleaseBuffer_g => true`, `ReleaseBytes_g => 16384`, `DenseOutput_g => true`
- `spp0`: `TxBufferBytes_g => 8192`, `RxBufferBytes_g => 8192`
- `nchar0`: none
- `spw0`: `LinkClkFreq_g => 200.0e6`, `RunDiv_g => 2`
- `auto_rst_sys`: `SyncTmr_g => true`

Constants with a field map (`fields` of the net):

- `spp0_S_Tx_User_s <= "0000000000000000000100100011"` (connection c3): 10:0 APID = 0x123; 11 Secondary header flag = '0'; 12 Packet type (telecommand) = '0'; 13 Packet name instead of sequence count = '0'; 27:14 Packet name = 0x0.
- `frm0_Cfg_Slot_s <= "00"`: 1:0 Key slot = 0.

## 4. Clocks and resets

| Clock domain | Frequency | Clock | Reset generator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| System clock (`sys`) | 100 MHz | top-level port `Clk_sys` | `auto_rst_sys` (olo_base_reset_gen, output `auto_rst_sys_RstOut_s`) |
| Link clock (`link`) | 200 MHz | top-level port `Clk_link` | none: no block of the domain has a synchronous reset |

Reset ports (`reset` of the port):

| Port | Reset | Actual | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frm0.Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_sys_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain System clock (clock Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_sys. |
| `ocr0.Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_sys_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain System clock (clock Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_sys. |
| `spp0.Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_sys_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain System clock (clock Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_sys. |
| `nchar0.Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_sys_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain System clock (clock Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_sys. |
| `spw0.Rst` | asynchronous | `Rst` | Asynchronous reset; the core synchronises its release in every domain. |
| `auto_rst_sys.RstIn` | asynchronous | `Rst` | Asynchronous reset input (polarity from RstInPolarity_g). |

`Rst` is the asynchronous system reset. A reset generator asserts the reset of its domain at once and releases it synchronously to the clock; a block with an asynchronous reset synchronises the release itself.

## 5. Constraints

Every clock crossing is an Open Logic block. Between the clocks of a crossing a maximum delay applies in both directions, the period of the faster clock, data path only (Open Logic clock crossing principles). Do not declare these clocks as asynchronous clock groups: in Vivado `set_clock_groups -asynchronous` overrides the delay limits.

- False path from `Rst`: Asynchronous reset input; the reset generators synchronise its release.
- False path from `spw0_Spw_DIn`, `spw0_Spw_SIn`: Inputs that spw0 synchronises itself.
- Output registers in the I/O blocks for `spw0_Spw_DOut`, `spw0_Spw_SOut`: Place the output flip-flops of data and strobe in the I/O blocks with matched routing.
- Maximum delay from the clock of `Clk_link` to the clock of `Clk_sys`: 5 ns, data path only (`set_max_delay -datapath_only` in Vivado). Clock crossings of spw0: the period of the faster clock.
- Maximum delay from the clock of `Clk_sys` to the clock of `Clk_link`: 5 ns, data path only (`set_max_delay -datapath_only` in Vivado). Clock crossings of spw0: the period of the faster clock.
- AMD Vivado: source the script of Open Logic once. It reads the scoped constraints of olo_base_cc_reset, olo_base_cc_bits, olo_base_cc_simple, olo_base_reset_gen and olo_base_ram_sdp wherever the system uses them, also inside the cores. tools/vivado/all_constraints_amd.tcl would also read those of olo_intf_sync, which expect device pins at its input and stop the build (ERROR 18-513) where a block synchronises internal signals with it, as ofb_pa_gty does; a block that synchronises device pins declares its own false path for them. File `src/base/tcl/olo_base_constraints_amd.tcl` of Open Logic.

## 6. Notes from the user guides

**Chunk framer** (`ocr_framer`, `frm0`): https://openspacehdl.org/opencrypto/docs/user_guide.html

- The slot Cfg_Slot is loaded for generated IVs and stays unchanged while the framer holds chunks.
- Every chunk consumes one invocation of the slot; save the counter regularly (GCM 9.1).
- A receiver decrypts every chunk on its own (IV bytes 0 to 11, AAD bytes 12 to 15, tag the last 16 bytes), orders the chunks by the invocation counter and finds the packet boundaries in the positions.

**AES-GCM core** (`ocr_core`, `ocr0`): https://openspacehdl.org/opencrypto/docs/user_guide.html

- Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen with SyncTmr_g = true.
- After the reset the key table erases every slot (NumKeys_g cycles, STATUS.BUSY = '1'); no key survives a reset.
- One context per message, in the order of the messages; the core pairs the n-th context with the n-th message.
- Load every key slot in use through the registers before sending contexts (programming sequence of the user guide).
- Without the release buffer, discard every decrypted message whose last beat carries the error flag or whose status is not OK.
- Save the invocation counter of every slot with generated IVs regularly ahead of the operational value (GCM 9.1).

**Space Packet node** (`spp_core`, `spp0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openspp/docs/user_guide.html

- Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen.
- After the reset the core initialises both APID tables (2048 clock cycles); packets are sent and delivered once the tables are ready.
- Serve every receive port, or place a buffer behind a port whose user can stall for long.
- TxBufferBytes_g holds the longest SDU of a port, RxBufferBytes_g the longest Space Packet.
- Hold the side band (TUser) of a send port constant during an SDU.
- A last beat without valid bytes (Keep all zero) ends an SDU or packet at the inputs; an SDU without any byte is rejected (0x02). The outputs never carry a beat without valid bytes.
- The user supplies the packet secondary header at the start of the Octet String and keeps the secondary header flag of an APID static.

**N-Char adapter** (`spp_nchar`, `nchar0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openspp/docs/user_guide.html

- A received end of packet marker without data characters is discarded.
- A link packet that ends with a beat without valid bytes gets its marker after the bytes of the earlier beats; a link packet without any byte sends nothing.

**SpaceWire port** (`owr_core`, `spw0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openwire/docs/user_guide.html

- LVDS output buffers for data and strobe and LVDS input buffers with fail-safe biasing belong to the top level; the core contains no I/O buffer.
- Enable the safe implementation of state machines in the synthesis tool.
- Set INT_HOLDOFF and INT_ACK_DELAY for the network before distributed interrupts are used.
- Serve the indication ports before the indication FIFO (16 entries) fills.
- Write registers as 32-bit words; a read that depends on a write waits for the write response.

## 7. Initialisation by software

Register addresses are byte addresses of the AXI4-Lite port of the block; write registers as 32-bit words and wait for the write response before a read that depends on it.

**`frm0`** (Chunk framer, `ocr_framer`):

1. Load the key slot Cfg_Slot of the AES-GCM core for generated IVs (KEY_LOAD with IV_GEN = '1', see the core) before the first packet; without a loaded slot every chunk fails with KEY.

**`ocr0`** (AES-GCM core, `ocr_core`) through the top-level ports `ocr_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x000): it reads 0x4F435201.
2. After the reset wait until STATUS (0x014) bit 0 BUSY is 0: the key table erases every slot.
3. Load every key slot in use: write the key to KEY0 to KEY7 (0x040 + 4 n; key byte 4 n in bits 31:24; 4, 6 or 8 words), for generated IVs the fixed field to IV_FIXED (0x060) and the first invocation counter to IV_COUNT_LO (0x064) and IV_COUNT_HI (0x068), then write KEY_LOAD (0x06C) with START (bit 31), IV_GEN (bit 8) and the slot (bits 7:0), for example 0x80000100 for slot 0 with generated IVs; wait until STATUS.BUSY is 0.

**`spp0`** (Space Packet node, `spp_core`) through the top-level ports `spp_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x000): it reads 0x53505001.
2. After the reset wait until TABLE_STATUS (0x040) bits 1:0 (TX_BUSY, RX_BUSY) are 0: the core initialises both APID tables (2048 clock cycles).
3. Nothing else is needed: with TxPathDefault_g and RxPathDefault_g every APID has an enabled path to destination 0 and to receive port 0, destination 0 has the Target Logical Address 0xFE (DEST_CTRL 0x400) and the own address is Tla_g. A flight configuration writes the APID tables (TX_TABLE_APID 0x030 and TX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x034, RX_TABLE_APID 0x038 and RX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x03C) and the destinations (DEST_CTRL 0x400 + 0x20 n).

**`spw0`** (SpaceWire port, `owr_core`) through the top-level ports `spw_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x00): it reads 0x4F575201.
2. Optionally write LINK_SPEED (0x14) bits 7:0 RUN_DIV: the bit period in the Run state in LinkClk cycles (reset value RunDiv_g); choose it for the far end, which samples at most about LinkClk / 1.2.
3. Write PORT_CTRL (0x10) = 0x34 (RECEIVER_EN, DRIVER_EN, LINK_START) to start the link, or 0x38 (AUTO_START) to wait for the far end.
4. Wait for PORT_STATUS (0x18) bits 2:0 LINK_STATE = 5 (Run) before packets are exchanged.

## 8. Checks

- Note: ocr0.M_Out has user; spp0.S_Tx[0] gets the side band constants of c3 instead.
- Note: spp0 sends Space Packets of up to ChunkBytes_g + 38 = 4134 bytes: the node that receives them needs RxBufferBytes_g of at least 4134 (spp0 has 8192).

## 9. Verification

A smoke testbench `encrypted_spp_over_spw_tb` (VHDL-2008, no extra libraries):

1. Instantiate `encrypted_spp_over_spw` and drive `Clk_sys` at 100 MHz, `Clk_link` at 200 MHz.
2. Hold `Rst` at '1' for 16 cycles of the slowest clock (100 MHz), then '0'.
3. Keep every external input idle: stream inputs with valid at '0', ready inputs of external outputs at '1', bus requests idle, pins at '0'.
4. Run for at least 100 us (the blocks initialise their tables after the reset) and stop the simulation: it must end without failed assertions, and the handshake outputs of the top level (valid, ready) and the line outputs must not be 'U' or 'X' after the reset. Data outputs may stay undefined while their valid is '0'.
5. Where an AXI4-Lite port is external, read the ID register of the block (section 7) and compare it with the documented value.

With GHDL: analyse the libraries of section 1, then `ghdl -i --std=08 -frelaxed encrypted_spp_over_spw.vhd encrypted_spp_over_spw_tb.vhd`, `ghdl -m --std=08 -frelaxed encrypted_spp_over_spw_tb` and `ghdl -r --std=08 -frelaxed encrypted_spp_over_spw_tb --stop-time=100us --assert-level=error --ieee-asserts=disable` (`--ieee-asserts=disable` silences the warnings of the numeric package about metavalues before the reset).

Optional end-to-end test, after the initialisation of section 7:

- AES-GCM core (`ocr_core`): Load the key slot, send a packet and check the output: with generated IVs the first 4 bytes of every message are IV_FIXED, the next 8 the invocation counter; decrypt it with AES-GCM in the test bench (or a second core) and compare.
- Space Packet node (`spp_core`): Send one SDU on a send port (APID 0x123, for example) and expect it on receive port 0 with the same APID in user bits 10:0, once the APID tables are ready.
- SpaceWire port (`owr_core`): Loop the SpaceWire line back (Spw_DOut to Spw_DIn, Spw_SOut to Spw_SIn) or connect a second port, start the link and wait for PORT_STATUS LINK_STATE = 5 (Run).

blocks.endToEnd: Loop the SpaceWire line back (Spw_DOut to Spw_DIn, Spw_SOut to Spw_SIn) or connect a second port, start the link and wait for PORT_STATUS LINK_STATE = 5 (Run).

generics.name: LinkClkFreq_g
generics.label: Link clock frequency
generics.description: Frequency of LinkClk. It must lie within 10 % of a multiple of 10 MHz, so that 10 Mb/s +/- 10 % can be reached with an integer divider.

generics.name: TxFifoDepth_g
generics.label: Transmit FIFO depth
generics.description: Depth of the transmit FIFO in N-Chars (power of 2).

generics.name: RxFifoDepth_g
generics.label: Receive FIFO depth
generics.description: Depth of the receive FIFO in N-Chars (power of 2); 64 or more allows seven outstanding FCTs.

generics.name: TimeCodes_g
generics.label: Time-code service
generics.description: Enables the time-code service and its ports.

generics.name: Interrupts_g
generics.label: Interrupt service
generics.description: Enables the distributed interrupt service and its ports.

generics.name: IntTimerWidth_g
generics.label: Interrupt timer width
generics.description: Width of the minimum interval and acknowledgement delay of the interrupt service

generics.name: LinkDisabled_g
generics.label: Link disabled after reset
generics.description: Reset value of LinkDisabled.

generics.name: LinkStart_g
generics.label: Link start after reset
generics.description: Reset value of LinkStart; the port starts the link without software.

generics.name: AutoStart_g
generics.label: Auto start after reset
generics.description: Reset value of AutoStart; the port starts the link when the far end does.

generics.name: RunDiv_g
generics.label: Run divider
generics.description: Reset value of the bit period in the Run state in LinkClk cycles.

generics.name: SyncStages_g
generics.label: Synchroniser stages
generics.description: Synchroniser stages of data and strobe.

clocks.label: User
clocks.description: Packet and broadcast service ports (any frequency).

clocks.label: Link
clocks.description: Encoding and data link layers; the transmit bit period is n LinkClk periods (n = 1 to 255).

resets.description: Asynchronous reset; the core synchronises its release in every domain.

interfaces.name: M_Pkt
interfaces.label: Received packets
interfaces.description: Must be served; the port gives credit only for free places of the receive FIFO.

blocks.name: Reset generator
blocks.summary: Synchronises an asynchronous reset to a clock and stretches it; optionally triplicated synchronisers.
